Seasonal rules for the handlers
This section explains the steps that matter
Companion Animal Travel Desk seasonal handling rules

This section keeps the desk on track when animal travel gets busy and the welcome team must move fast without losing care. Aurelia Skyways treats each journey as shared work, so every record, crate check, and handoff needs clear attention from the first contact to boarding.

Desk staff must confirm the travel file, carrier setup, and animal condition before the passenger reaches the gate area. If a pet arrives stressed, the handler should slow the process, steady the tone, and bring in the senior coordinator when needed. The traveler should get simple directions, and the desk should keep the notes clean, brief, and easy to follow. If the animal has a name on the file, use it as listed and do not improvise. This is especially important when the same route has several pet moves in a row and the welcome team is already under strain.

Any concern about food, water, temperature, noise, or carrier security must be raised at once. The desk does not guess, and it does not pass a doubtful case along without a clear note. If a carrier seal looks weak or the paperwork does not match the animal, hold the handoff and alert the lead checker. When a traveler asks for help, answer in plain words and keep the focus on safe boarding, calm movement, and exact records.

After the animal has moved on, close the file with the final status, any issue seen, and the name of the staff member who completed the check. If the desk sees a repeat problem, flag it right away so the next shift does not walk blind into the same mess. For urgent follow-up, contact the senior coordinator at the Companion Animal Travel Desk.
